title: Bivariate Bicycle Codes and Metachecks: Syndrome Repair, Measurement-Fault Ambiguity, and Logical Obstructions
abstract: Faulty syndrome measurements can corrupt an otherwise correct quantum-error correction step. Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes contain dependent stabilizer checks, so their measured syndromes obey parity constraints that can be used as metachecks. We study when this built-in redundancy actually supports syndrome repair and how it interacts with the logical structure of the code. Annihilator quotients identify single-block logical classes and show when a mixed-block search is unavoidable. For syndrome repair, the metasyndrome is equivalent to reduction modulo the valid-syndrome ideal. The translation group therefore maps into the unit group of a quotient algebra of dimension $k/2$, with kernel $K_M$. This gives a distance-two characterization, a unit-group bound on distinguishable single faults, and a family-level obstruction: for bounded-$k$ BB families with growing block length, metasyndrome-only exact repair fails with probability tending to one at any fixed measurement-error rate. With no intervening data fault, the same orbit count also gives the minimum partial second measurement needed to remove every single-fault ambiguity. Exact calculations separate the standard examples. The $[[72,12,6]]$ code has syndrome distance three and minimum-weight repair corrects every single measurement fault, whereas Gross $[[144,12,12]]$ has 36 indistinguishable single-fault pairs. Sustained phenomenological experiments show the same qualitative contrast and favor joint data--measurement decoding over a separated repair stage on the codes with stronger ambiguity. The analysis extends our earlier coprime-period treatment to general two-block BB codes and separates measurement ambiguity from the data error it can induce.
summary: This paper analyzes Bivariate Bicycle codes to understand how built-in redundancy (metachecks) can be used for syndrome repair in quantum error correction. It shows that theoretical limitations exist for metasyndrome-only repair, especially as codes scale. The findings strongly favor joint decoding strategies over separated repair stages in the presence of measurement noise.
main_problem: The paper investigates syndrome repair in quantum error correction codes, specifically analyzing how built-in redundancy (metachecks) in Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes handles measurement-fault ambiguity.
main_result: Metasyndrome-only exact repair fails for bounded-$k$ BB families with growing block length, suggesting that joint data–measurement decoding is superior to separated repair stages when ambiguity is high.
method: The authors employ algebraic tools, including quotient algebras and the analysis of translation groups, to characterize the constraints imposed by metachecks on measured syndromes.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes within the Calderbank–Shor–Steane (CSS) stabilizer formalism, analyzing their syndrome code ($S$) and metacheck space ($C_M$).
key_observables: Metasyndrome ($	ext{Mes}$), syndrome distance ($d_S$), unit group size (bounding single faults), and the failure probability in sustained-memory experiments.
important_parameters: Measurement-error rate ($p$), code parameters (e.g., $[[72, 12, 6]]$), and the block length/code family structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis separates logical operators and measurement-side redundancy, and the sustained-memory experiment uses independent Bernoulli data and measurement faults.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the extraction process of the syndrome code and metachecks, while tables provide comprehensive notation and specific code examples.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining the algebraic structure of BB codes and their redundancy (metachecks) to deriving the metasyndrome, establishing theoretical bounds on fault distinguishability, and concluding with phenomenological experiments comparing decoding strategies.
why_interesting: The rigorous algebraic framework connecting syndrome redundancy to physical error correction limitations provides deep insights into the practical limits of quantum memory and fault tolerance.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Logical and syndrome calculations used in the paper. The two sides are kept separate because syndrome redundancy does not determine quantum distance, and quantum distance does not determine the reliability of syndrome repair.

Fig. 2. Extraction of the syndrome code and metachecks from a BB code. The generators a and b determine the multiplication matrices and hence the selected CSS check matrix H. Its image is the valid-syndrome code S, whereas the kernel of H⊤gives the metacheck space CM. Choosing a basis of CM gives the metacheck matrix M. For a noisy measurement es = He+ξ, the relation MH = 0 removes the data contribution, leaving the metasyndrome Mes = Mξ.
Fig. 3. Left-block quotient. The outer space contains errors invisible to the selected syndrome; quotienting by the exact stabilizer slice leaves logical classes.

Fig. 4. Exact minimum-weight syndrome-repair failure on a denser measurement-noise grid. The [[72, 12, 6]] curve begins quadratically with coefficient 603. For Gross and BB(6, 3), the black curves show the finite-rate orbit bounds for metasyndrome-only exact repair, 1 −(1 −pM)36 and 1 −(1 −pM)9, from Corollary 6. These finite-rate bounds remain distinct from the exact curves away from the low-noise limit.

Fig. 5. Sustained phenomenological memory with R = 10 noisy rounds and one ideal final round. Markers are the observed effective rates εeff; connecting segments are guides between sampled physical error rates and are not fitted or smoothed. Light ribbons are 95% anytime-valid beta–binomial mixture confidence sequences, retained because the runs use adaptive stopping. Downward open triangles denote one-sided 95% upper limits for zero-failure runs. The dotted line is εeff = p. The separated BP+OSD repair variant is omitted here for clarity; its single-fault behavior is reported exhaustively in Table VIII. Saturated points with block failure above 0.95 are not shown.
